## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Jāgarajātaka* (Ja 414), rendered in English as "Who Wakes?", is a narrative included in the canonical Pali *Jātaka* collection [SuttaCentral]. In the commentary edited by V. Fausböll, the tale is framed by the Buddha dwelling at Jetavana, delivered on account of a certain lay follower (*upāsaka*) and stream-enterer (*sotāpanna*) who travelled from Sāvatthī with a caravan along a desert track [Fausböll 1883; SuttaCentral]. The core verse discourse opens with the riddle or inquiry *Ko dha jāgarataṃ sutto* ("Who wakes while sleeping?") [Fausböll 1883; SuttaCentral]. In the narrative of the past, the Bodhisatta was an ascetic (*tāpaso*) who answered a deity (*devatā*); after offering praise to the Bodhisatta, the deity returned to her celestial mansion (*vimāna*). In the concluding identification (*samodhāna*), the Buddha reveals that the deity was Uppalavaṇṇā and the ascetic was the Bodhisatta himself [Fausböll 1883].

DharmaNexus also detects ten low-confidence cross-language alignments (maximum score 15) with a Tibetan translation of the *Pramāṇavārttikālaṃkāraṭīkā-supariśuddhā* (D4226-3), though these are machine matches rather than historical parallels [DharmaNexus]. SuttaCentral identifies no verified parallels in other canonical collections and records four translations across four languages [SuttaCentral].
